# Build: api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T21:02:31.264Z
> I don't want to have to approve builds sent to API. They need to just go there just like any other build.

## What to build
Continue build "API accounts need no approval: builds route there like any other account (spend caps still apply)" (api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 21:02):
"I don't want to have to approve builds sent to API. They need to just go there just like any other build."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Remove the owner-click requirement for routing builds to API-key accounts (pipeline_route api, overflow, voice/API). API accounts are treated like any other account in the order: builds go there automatically with no approval. Keep the daily/weekly spend caps and the 80% alert as the safety net; when a cap is hit, stop sending there and notify on AmberX. Supersedes the confirm-approval rule for API runs in token-usage-log s10.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) I don't want to have to approve builds sent to API. They need to just go there just like any other build.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link api-accounts-need-no-approval-builds-route-there --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T19:21:03.353Z
> Build queue doesn't open the orchestrator. It opens the old build queue.

## What to build
Continue build "Home page Build queue card opens the orchestrator, not the old build queue" (home-page-build-queue-card-opens-the-orchestrato) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 19:21):
"Build queue doesn't open the orchestrator. It opens the old build queue."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/home-page-build-queue-card-opens-the-orchestrato
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~1.8 h):
[ ] s1 (~25 min) Find every link to the old build queue screen (grep apps/console-web for the old queue route, view id and console_show/console_open targets, e.g. 'build-queue', 'queue', '#/builds/queue') and list them. Then point the Home page Build queue card and its link at the Build orchestrator screen (Pending / Queued / Building). Keep the card's counts reading from the orchestrator state (_claude/builds/orchestrator.json via its existing route), not the old queue store.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) API part for the changed card. Make the deep link console_show / console_open target 'orchestrator' (with optional tab=pending|queued|building) the canonical target. Alias the old build-queue targets to it so old links and old callers land on the orchestrator. Expose the Home card's state (counts per lane plus its target) through the console REST route, the MCP console actions, the CLI and the AmberX voice intent ('open build queue' / 'open orchestrator'), all four the same.
[ ] s3 (~25 min) Retire the rest of the old queue links found in step 1. Repoint nav, launcher tiles, command palette entries, notification and badge click targets, and doc and help links to the orchestrator. Make the old queue screen route redirect to the orchestrator instead of rendering, and remove dead references to it.
[ ] s4 (~25 min) Tests, report and PR. Add or adjust tests: the Home card href and target resolve to the orchestrator; the old build-queue targets and route redirect to it; REST, MCP, CLI and voice return the same card state and open the same target. Run the suites. Write _claude/builds/reports/home-page-build-queue-card-opens-the-orchestrato.md, add the THREADS row in _claude/THREADS.md, and open the PR, saying how the card is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.detail: When a build session stops on its own with steps left (outcome 'returned'), the dispatcher puts the build straight back in the Queue (keeping its priority and position) instead of Pending, and continues from the next step. Only after 3 consecutive early stops with no step progress does it go to Pending, with an AmberX notification and the reason. Fold into the stall watchdog build.
